summary: One of the world's densest startup ecosystems, centred on Tel Aviv, Jerusalem and Haifa; strong in cyber, AI, semiconductors, fintech and defence tech. Major exits include Wiz (Google), Mobileye and Waze.
startup_visa: Innovation Visa for Foreign Technology Entrepreneurs (B/2 up to 24 months via IIA landing-pad incubators, then expert visa), https://innovationisrael.org.il/en/programs/tech-innovation-visa/
company_setup: Ltd (private company) registered with the Israeli Corporations Authority; can be done remotely via a local lawyer, typically 1-2 weeks and a few thousand US$ in fees. Many founders use a Delaware C-corp with an Israeli subsidiary.

grants.name: Ideation (Tnufa) Incentive Program
grants.amount: conditional grant up to NIS 200k (80% of budget)

grants.name: Technological Incubators Program
grants.amount: up to 85% of budget, up to NIS 3.5M over 2 years
grants.eligibility: early-stage deep-tech startups admitted by an IIA-franchised incubator

grants.name: Startup Fund Pre-Seed/Seed track

grants.eligibility: Israeli startups raising with qualifying investors

grants.name: Ideation (Tnufa) Challenge - Critical Minerals

grants.name: From Development to Manufacturing (MOFET)
grants.eligibility: Israeli tech companies moving to production

summary: Amman-centred ecosystem with strong software, gaming and e-commerce talent; exits include Maktoob (Yahoo) and Jamalon. The World Bank-backed ISSF fund of funds anchors local VC.
startup_visa: none (investor residency via Ministry of Investment; no dedicated startup visa verified)
company_setup: LLC or Private Shareholding Company registered with the Companies Control Department; foreigners can own most tech businesses; about 1-2 weeks.

grants.name: Innovative Startups and SMEs Fund (ISSF)
grants.agency: ISSF / World Bank / Central Bank of Jordan
grants.amount: fund of funds and co-investment, US$148M AUM
grants.eligibility: Jordanian startups via partner VCs; direct co-investments

resources.name: Ministry of Digital Economy and Entrepreneurship

notes: Flat6Labs Amman's last published deadline was Feb 2025. Regional conflict has dampened 2024-26 funding.

summary: Beirut historically had a vibrant scene (Anghami listed on Nasdaq) but the 2019 banking collapse, 2020 port blast and 2024 war hit it hard; many startups now operate from the Gulf or Europe.
company_setup: SAL or SARL via notary and commercial register; capital controls make local banking hard, so many founders incorporate abroad (UAE, Delaware) and keep a Lebanese subsidiary.

grants.name: Kafalat loan guarantees (Innovative / Kafalat Plus)
grants.amount: guaranteed bank loans for SMEs and innovative startups

accelerators.name: Berytech
accelerators.investment: grants and seed via partners, no equity for most

notes: Financial crisis since 2019 (BDL Circular 331 VC scheme is effectively defunct). Funding is scarce; status of Flat6Labs Beirut unclear and omitted.

summary: Tiny, fragile ecosystem emerging after the Dec 2024 change of government; most Syrian founders operate from Turkey, Jordan, the Gulf or Europe. Reconstruction and diaspora returns are early signals.
company_setup: Companies register via the Ministry of Economy; banking links remain limited. Most founders use a diaspora entity (UAE, Turkey, Estonia e-Residency, Delaware).

resources.name: Jusoor
resources.note: diaspora NGO for education and entrepreneurship

notes: Sanctions: US lifted most Syria sanctions in mid-2025 and the EU eased economic sanctions, but compliance risk, de-risking by banks and conflict persist. No verified active accelerators or VCs inside Syria as of Oct 2026.

summary: Small tech scene in Ramallah, Nablus and (formerly) Gaza, focused on outsourcing and software; severely disrupted by the Gaza war since Oct 2023 and West Bank restrictions.
company_setup: Companies register with the Ministry of National Economy; movement and banking constraints lead many founders to incorporate in Jordan, UAE or Delaware.

resources.name: UNDP Programme of Assistance to the Palestinian People

notes: War in Gaza since Oct 2023 has destroyed much infrastructure; Gaza Sky Geeks operates largely remotely/online. Ibtikar Fund II raised a US$15M first close.

summary: Fast-growing but early ecosystem in Baghdad, Erbil and Basra, driven by a young population, fintech and delivery apps; heavily cash-based economy.
company_setup: LLC registration with the Companies Registrar (Baghdad) or KRG; foreigners usually need a local partner or investment licence; several weeks.

grants.name: Riyada initiative (SME lending)
grants.amount: subsidised SME and startup loans via banks

notes: Security and political risk; Iraqi Development Fund status not verified and omitted.

summary: MENA's largest VC market by funding since 2023, centred on Riyadh, driven by Vision 2030, SVC fund-of-funds and Monsha'at; strengths in fintech, e-commerce, logistics and AI. Notable: Tabby, Tamara, Jahez IPO.
startup_visa: Entrepreneur licence via Ministry of Investment (MISA) plus Premium Residency entrepreneur category, https://misa.gov.sa/
company_setup: LLC with MISA licence for foreign owners (100% foreign ownership allowed in most sectors), commercial registration via Saudi Business Center; 1-4 weeks.

grants.name: SVC fund-of-funds and co-investment programs

summary: Small but wealthy market; notable startups include Talabat and Carriage (both acquired). Government National Fund for SMEs and family offices are main funders.
company_setup: WLL via Ministry of Commerce; 100% foreign ownership possible via KDIPA licence; several weeks.

summary: Muscat-centred ecosystem backed by state funds (Oman Technology Fund, Future Fund Oman) and the SME Development Authority; focus on logistics, energy and tourism tech.
company_setup: LLC via Invest Easy portal; 100% foreign ownership allowed in most sectors; 1-2 weeks.

grants.name: Future Fund Oman (SME and startup allocation)

summary: Fragile, conflict-affected economy with a very small number of tech startups, mostly in Sanaa and Aden; support comes from donor-funded small-business programs.
company_setup: Registration is split between rival authorities; most founders use a diaspora entity (Saudi, UAE, Estonia e-Residency, Delaware).

grants.agency: Small and Micro Enterprise Promotion Service

summary: MENA's leading startup hub (Dubai, Abu Dhabi) with heavy state support, free zones and global talent; notable exits Careem (Uber) and Souq (Amazon). Strong in fintech, AI and proptech.
startup_visa: Golden Visa (entrepreneur and skilled categories, 5-10 years), https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/visa-and-emirates-id/residence-visas/golden-visa
company_setup: Free-zone LLC (DIFC, ADGM, DMCC, Hub71/ADGM, in5) or mainland LLC with 100% foreign ownership; can largely be done remotely in 1-3 weeks; US$3k-15k/year.

summary: State-driven ecosystem around QSTP, Qatar Development Bank and the QIA US$1B fund-of-funds program; growing in fintech, sportstech and AI. Startup Qatar (Invest Qatar) is the one-stop portal.
startup_visa: none dedicated; Startup Qatar portal facilitates residency for founders, https://startupqatar.qa/en
company_setup: LLC via Ministry of Commerce or free-zone entity (QFC, QSTP, Qatar Free Zones); 100% foreign ownership in many sectors; 2-4 weeks.

summary: Compact, regulator-friendly hub for fintech (CBB sandbox, Bahrain FinTech Bay) with strong Tamkeen subsidies and the Al Waha fund of funds.
startup_visa: Golden Residency (investor/talent categories); no dedicated startup visa
company_setup: WLL or SPC via Sijilat portal; 100% foreign ownership in most sectors; can be done in days, largely remotely.

company_setup: LLC or JSC via GAFI one-stop shop; 100% foreign ownership allowed; 1-3 weeks; many founders also use Delaware/UAE holdcos.

summary: Very early ecosystem in Tripoli and Benghazi, supported mainly by NGOs and donors; e-payments and delivery apps are emerging.

summary: Very small digital ecosystem in Nouakchott; growth tied to mobile money and gas projects. Support mainly from donors.
company_setup: SARL via the one-stop guichet unique of APIM; low capital requirement; diaspora entities common.
notes: No verified local accelerators or VCs; regional funds (Partech Africa, Seedstars) rarely invest here.

summary: Disputed territory; the Moroccan-administered areas (Laayoune, Dakhla) follow Moroccan programs; essentially no startup ecosystem in Polisario-held areas.
company_setup: In Moroccan-administered areas, companies register under Moroccan law via regional investment centres.
notes: Sovereignty disputed (UN non-self-governing territory); Moroccan national programs (Tamwilcom, Maroc PME) apply in administered areas. EU court rulings affect trade.

summary: Large ecosystem led by Istanbul with Ankara and Izmir; gaming is a standout (Peak, Dream Games, Rollic), plus fintech and e-commerce (Getir, Trendyol). Strong state grants via TUBITAK and KOSGEB and 90+ technoparks.
startup_visa: Turkiye Tech Visa (founders and tech talent), https://www.turkiyetechvisa.gov.tr/
company_setup: Ltd. Sti. or A.S. via trade registry; 100% foreign ownership allowed; about 1 week; technopark companies get tax exemptions.
notes: Lira volatility makes TRY amounts shrink in US$. BiGG+ Tohum window 5 Oct - 20 Nov 2026 reported via search; confirm on PRODIS.

summary: Large, isolated domestic tech market (Tehran) with local champions like Digikala, Snapp and Cafe Bazaar, supported by the knowledge-based company law and state innovation funds.
company_setup: Private joint-stock or LLC via Iran's companies registration office; foreign founders face severe sanctions and banking barriers.
